about.title: Salinas Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Salinas takes many shapes: field crews and packing lines, warehouse floors, construction sites, delivery routes that run up N Main Street and across E Market Street, E Laurel Drive and E Boronda Road. Each of those settings carries its own way of getting hurt, and each raises the same first question under California law. Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, and it pays regardless of who caused the accident. That coverage matters, but it is also limited. If someone other than your employer contributed to the injury, a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a faulty machine, or another driver, a separate claim against that third party may be available. Those claims run on a two-year clock in California. Two practical points for Monterey County workers: tell your employer about the injury within 30 days, and know that retaliation for reporting is illegal. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles cases like yours on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on comp versus a third-party claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is typically your only route against the employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or driver can be pursued separately. An attorney can tell you early whether that second path exists.

items.title: Deadlines handled from day one
items.desc: California expects you to notify your employer within 30 days, and third-party injury claims carry a two-year filing deadline. The attorneys we connect you with build those dates into the plan from the start.

items.title: Protection if your job pushes back
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury is against California law. Speaking with an independent attorney gives you someone to turn to if hours are cut, duties change, or pressure follows your report.

items.question: I was hit while driving a work van on E Market Street. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation generally covers medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. If another driver was negligent, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver, which is handled outside the comp system and subject to the two-year deadline. Salinas recorded 410 injury collisions in 2025, many peaking on Friday evenings, so work-related crashes are not unusual here.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury at a Salinas packing plant or farm?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits an employer from retaliating against you for reporting a work injury or filing a workers' comp claim. You should still make the report within 30 days to protect your benefits. If you notice your shifts disappearing or your role changing after a report, an attorney can help you document what is happening.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our connection service is free, and we are not a law firm ourselves. The independent attorneys in our network take injury cases on contingency, which means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. You can ask questions before deciding whether to move forward.
